web_blocks.html: State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLV) provides 0.08%-expense access to 61 profitable S&P 500 healthcare leaders ($46.57B AUM, 0.01% spread, 1.44% yield, ~21.5% look-through FCF margin) [1][9]. Pass 1 business quality earns COMPOUNDER_PASS with PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health. Watch flags cover 60.64% top-10 concentration (16.78% LLY) [31], 40 IRA drugs selected through 2028 [14], Merck's December 2028 Keytruda cliff [20][36], UNH's 88.4% MCR and FTC/DOJ scrutiny [35][37], and Big-Three wholesaler concentration [34].

At the verified 2026-11-20 close of $177.24 (with the 2026-11-23 live snapshot showing $179.09 on TradingView and $179.44 on Finviz; +1.04% 1D / -5.99% 1W on Nov 23), XLV holds STAGE_2 inside its $175.46–$180.80 support zone (+1.34% above 50D SMA $176.73). Meanwhile, the U.S. market sits in a confirmed Downtrend (38.8% >50DMA, 10 distribution days) and our portfolio cash is 9.13% ($7,290.91 of $79,861.16 NAV vs. 22.0% floor). Because an 8% multiple haircut collapses support asymmetry to 0.06:1, we tighten our dual verdict to New Capital: WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (TIER_2, CORE_ALPHA) ($175.46–$180.80 support zone, ratcheted stop $164.19, base target $206.00) until breadth >50DMA tops 45% and cash rebuilds toward 22.0%, while Current Position: NOT_HELD (0 shares).

web_blocks.text: 0.2 The Debate in One Minute & Dual-Date Gate Disclosure

web_blocks.html: Bulls point to 13.47% projected 3–5Y EPS growth [2], Eli Lilly's $16.08B quarterly GLP-1 run-rate [33], and UNH's 14.5x forward multiple reset. Bears highlight the 10-distribution-day Downtrend (38.8% >50DMA), 5.04% 10-year Treasury yields, 40 IRA drugs [14], FTC/DOJ PBM scrutiny [35][37], and Merck's 2028 Keytruda cliff [36]. Dual-Date Note: Decisions anchor to the verified 2026-11-20 close ($177.24), while the 2026-11-23 live TradingView/Finviz snapshot ($179.09 / $179.44; +1.04% 1D, -5.99% 1W) confirms Stage 2 support [$175.46, $180.80] and the $164.19 stop.

Chapters 1–6 audit XLV's index plumbing, 61-stock mix, 0.08% fee economics, and 10-year constituent cash flows without price bias. Chapters 7–9 then integrate valuation ($177.24 vs. 5.04% 10Y yield, plus an -8% multiple stress test), Stage 2 technicals ($175.46–$180.80 zone, $164.19 stop), our declined options check (NO_OPTIONS_EDGE), and our 100%-reconciled 100% CASH redeployment plan.

Discipline around portfolio cash remains central to this refresh. With $7,290.91 in cash representing just 9.13% of our $79,861.16 NAV against a 22.0% Downtrend floor, we decline illiquid LEAPS options and stage spot XLV entries strictly inside $175.46–$180.80 only after 4H/daily reversals confirm.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our refreshed institutional underwriting dossier on the State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF, ticker XLV. Every baseline chapter has been challenged against new Q3 2026 SEC filings, FTC enforcement disclosures, and live November 2026 market structure.

Here is our verdict up front. On business quality, XLV earns Compounder Pass with Pass With Watch KPI health. Although XLV holds Stage 2 support inside $175.46–$180.80 ($177.24 verified 2026-11-20 close; $179.09 TradingView live snapshot on 2026-11-23), the U.S. market remains in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend and portfolio cash sits at 9.13% against a 22.0% floor. We therefore rate XLV WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (TIER_2) with a ratcheted $164.19 stop and $206.00 base target while current holdings remain NOT_HELD (0 shares).

book_subsections.title: Before We Begin Chapter 1
paragraphs: Every figure in this monograph is anchored to primary SEC filings, State Street holdings data, and the November 20, 2026 session cutoff alongside our November 23 live snapshot check. Let us walk through the evidence chapter by chapter.

Keep two guardrails in mind as you read. First, we never compromise on position sizing in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend when portfolio cash is below the 22.0% floor. Second, we let our ratcheted $164.19 stop and $175.46–$180.80 support zone govern every trade with zero FOMO.

Notice also why we compare XLV against both peer healthcare ETFs and its top-ten constituents. With Eli Lilly at 16.78% weight, Johnson & Johnson at 10.15%, AbbVie at 7.87%, Merck at 5.14%, and UnitedHealth at 4.75%, XLV behaves like a barbell between GLP-1 growth and discounted Managed Care.
Let us begin Chapter 1 by stripping away the ticker price and examining XLV's 1998 Select Sector SPDR architecture from the ground up.

As you move through the first six chapters, pay close attention to two newly patched blind spots from our refresh audit: Big-Three pharmaceutical wholesaler concentration disclosed in Eli Lilly's FY2025 10-K, and active FTC/DOJ antitrust and Medicare Advantage enforcement facing UnitedHealth and the major PBMs. Understanding both risks up front makes our Chapters 7 through 9 valuation and risk plan far more durable.
